items.headline: StarHub to merge with M1 in a S$1.1 billion all-share deal by 2027
items.summary: StarHub and M1 owner Keppel announced an all-share merger valued at S$1.1 billion, creating a telco serving about 4.1 million customers. StarHub will also buy Circles.Life’s Singapore business, with completion expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.

items.headline: Singapore and Australia widen their supply-chain pact to cover food and semiconductors
items.summary: At a leaders’ retreat in Canberra, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Australian PM Anthony Albanese extended a bilateral memorandum to secure trade in essential goods, including food and semiconductors, and agreed to deepen cooperation on critical and emerging technologies such as AI.

items.headline: PM Wong says Singapore is working with the US to stop AI-chip re-routing
items.summary: Speaking in Canberra, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore is working with Washington to stop companies from exploiting the country to divert US artificial-intelligence chips to other destinations, rejecting the idea that Singapore is a conduit for sanctioned trade.

items.headline: First person charged under Singapore’s tougher Kpod laws jailed over three years
items.summary: A Singaporean man became the first person sentenced under tightened laws targeting etomidate-laced vape pods, known as Kpods, receiving three years, 10 months and two weeks’ jail plus two strokes of the cane, after Singapore reclassified etomidate as a controlled drug.

items.headline: Putin says Russian retaliation is ‘inevitable’ after Ukraine strikes oil refineries
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin said retaliatory action was ‘inevitable’ after Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries continued despite a plea from US President Donald Trump to halt them, casting fresh doubt over US-mediated efforts to restart peace talks.

items.headline: Ukraine says it struck a Russian warship off Libya in a drone attack
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s SBU intelligence service used sea drones to hit the Russian corvette Merkury at Libya’s Benghazi port, with satellite imagery showing the vessel largely capsized. Libya’s eastern authorities reported crew deaths and asked the UN to investigate.

items.headline: Israeli air strike kills a senior Hamas security official in Gaza
items.summary: An Israeli strike killed Brigadier General Naim Abu Nahl, head of Hamas’s internal security service, according to Gaza’s interior ministry, among seven people it said were killed on Tuesday. Gaza health officials also issued a meningitis alert as near-daily strikes continued despite the year-old ceasefire.

items.headline: Israel’s Eisenkot races a December 6 deadline to form a government
items.summary: Coalition talks between Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud ended without a deal over who would lead the country and whether Itamar Ben-Gvir would join. Eisenkot, tasked by the president after an inconclusive election, has until December 6 — extendable by 14 days — to assemble a majority.

items.headline: Walmart teams up with Meta to sell Black Friday deals through an AI agent
items.summary: Walmart said shoppers can now buy its Black Friday deals through Meta’s AI agent, Muse, browsing and checking out within a chat interface — the latest push to turn conversational assistants into shopping storefronts.

items.headline: EV-truck startup Harbinger lands over $100 million, backed by Palmer Luckey’s bank
items.summary: Electric commercial-truck maker Harbinger secured more than $100 million in new financing, including debt from Erebor, the bank founded by Palmer Luckey, as demand for medium-duty electric trucks picks up, TechCrunch reported.

items.headline: Anthropic shares fall below their IPO price days after going public
items.summary: Anthropic’s stock dropped below its $83 IPO price, trading as low as $76, less than a week after the AI company debuted on the Nasdaq at $111.50 a share, feeding worries about stretched valuations across AI startups.

items.headline: Supertake raises $20 million to turn market predictions into AI-built portfolios
items.summary: AI investing startup Supertake raised $20 million in seed funding led by Adjacent, with Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures participating, to let AI agents translate users’ market views into stock portfolios.

items.headline: Sanofi to buy Insmed for about $41 billion in biggest pharma deal since 2023
items.summary: France’s Sanofi agreed to acquire US biotech Insmed for $175 a share, or roughly $41 billion in cash, to offset the looming patent expiry of its top seller Dupixent. Insmed shares jumped about 14%; it is the largest pharma takeover since Pfizer bought Seagen in 2023.

items.headline: US readies tariff increases on China, the EU and a dozen more economies
items.summary: The US is preparing to raise tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies as soon as Tuesday, Bloomberg reported, unsettling markets already rattled by swings in AI stocks.

items.headline: US tech stocks slide as the Nvidia relief rally fades
items.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell about 2% on Tuesday and Nvidia dropped roughly 6%, giving back much of the previous day’s surge that followed Jensen Huang’s return as CEO, as investors refocused on stretched AI valuations and debt-funded data-center spending.

items.headline: Abercrombie jumps 21% on strong results as Analog Devices slides 18%
items.summary: Abercrombie & Fitch rose about 21% after third-quarter earnings beat expectations, while chipmaker Analog Devices fell roughly 18% despite topping estimates, as retailers outperformed a weak session for semiconductors.

items.headline: US consumer confidence rises in November even as inflation worries linger
items.summary: US consumer confidence improved in November, helped by easing political uncertainty after the midterm elections, though households stayed concerned about persistent inflation, CNBC reported.

items.headline: 🏎 F1 reaches Qatar with Red Bull holding a nine-point edge over McLaren for third
items.summary: Formula 1 heads to Lusail for the Qatar Grand Prix (Nov 27-29), the penultimate round, with the titles already settled — Kimi Antonelli is champion and Mercedes hold the constructors’ crown. The live fight is for third, where Red Bull (440 points) lead McLaren (431) with two races left.

items.headline: 🏎 FIA agrees a 2030 engine framework built around a turbocharged V8
items.summary: The FIA, Formula 1, teams and manufacturers reached unanimous agreement on a 2030 power-unit framework centred on a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 running on sustainable fuels — the first V8 since 2013 — paired with a lighter car. The rules still need final approval by the World Motorsport Council next month.

items.headline: 🏏 India and New Zealand head to Christchurch for the second Test
items.summary: India resume their series in New Zealand with the second Test at Christchurch, running Nov 27 to Dec 1, after the opener in Wellington ended in a draw. The match is part of the 2025-27 World Test Championship cycle.

items.headline: 🎾 Davis Cup Final 8 gets under way in Bologna with Italy defending
items.summary: The eight-nation Davis Cup Finals began in Bologna on Nov 24, running through Nov 29, with host nation Italy — the defending champions — opening their title defence against a field drawn from the November qualifiers.

items.headline: Sleuth finds ‘impossible proteins’ in hundreds of research papers
items.summary: A science-integrity sleuth flagged 230 reports across 221 papers published since 2004 that show proteins appearing in genetically altered cell lines that lack the genes to make them — a signal of likely errors or image manipulation, Nature reported.

items.headline: Webb telescope maps the dust that reveals a dying star’s final hours
items.summary: New mid-infrared images from the James Webb Space Telescope show the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant holds pockets of mostly silica dust alongside carbon-rich dust, pointing to a dramatic change inside the original star possibly just hours before it exploded.

items.headline: Scientists map how human sweat flips a switch that draws mosquitoes
items.summary: Researchers worked out 3D structures showing how acids in human sweat bind and open an ion-channel receptor in a malaria-carrying mosquito, triggering the signal that steers it toward people. The work could inspire new ways to blunt mosquito attraction, Nature reported.

items.headline: Study finds blood stem cells keep an ‘inflammatory memory’ of past infections
items.summary: Scientists identified a subset of human blood-forming stem cells that retain a durable molecular imprint of past inflammation, which researchers link to age-related immune decline and a higher risk of blood cancers.

fun_fact.headline: A newborn has about 300 bones but an adult has only 206
fun_fact.body: A newborn baby has about 300 bones, but an adult has only 206. As a child grows, many of the separate bones — especially in the skull, spine and pelvis — gradually fuse together, so we end up with fewer bones than we were born with.

puzzle.title: The Stopped Clock
puzzle.body:
A man’s only clock has stopped, and he has no watch, no phone and no other way to tell the time at home. He walks to a friend’s house some distance away, visits for a while, then walks home — never asking anyone the time and passing no other clock on the way. Yet the moment he gets home he can set his stopped clock to the correct time. How?

(Assume he walks at the same steady pace both ways.)
puzzle.approach: You can’t carry the time with you — but you can measure how long things take.
puzzle.answer:
Before leaving, he winds his stopped clock and starts it at any reading — say 12:00 — so it begins ticking.

At his friend’s house, which has a working clock, he notes the time he arrives and the time he leaves, so he knows exactly how long he stayed.

Back home, his own clock shows the total time elapsed since he left. Subtract the time spent at the friend’s house and what remains is the round-trip walking time; half of that is the one-way walk.

Correct time now = the time he left the friend’s house + the one-way walking time. He sets his clock to that.

word_puzzle.title: Square One
word_puzzle.body:
A 5×5 mini. Each row (Across) and each column (Down) spells a common five-letter word.

Grid (□ = empty cell):
[1]□ [2]□ [3]□ [4]□ [5]□
[6]□ □ □ □ □
[7]□ □ □ □ □
[8]□ □ □ □ □
[9]□ □ □ □ □

Across
1. Valentine’s symbol; the core of a matter
6. A fire’s last glowing coal
7. To mistreat
8. Pine-sap residue; a violin-bow coating
9. The latest direction in fashion

Down
1. ‘Cross your ___’
2. A dying fire’s faint glow
3. Misuse
4. Sticky secretion from a pine tree
5. A tendency that develops over time
word_puzzle.approach: Every across answer also reads down the matching column — it’s a symmetric 5×5 word square.
word_puzzle.answer:
Across — 1 HEART · 6 EMBER · 7 ABUSE · 8 RESIN · 9 TREND
Down — 1 HEART · 2 EMBER · 3 ABUSE · 4 RESIN · 5 TREND

Filled grid:
H E A R T
E M B E R
A B U S E
R E S I N
T R E N D

It’s a symmetric word square, so each across word also reads straight down its column.
